blocks.title: What not to do — five source-linked failure modes
blocks.content:
W&W synthesis — not an external source.

1. Decorative pastiche. Do not dress a single enormous enclosure in token Mission Revival arches or barracks windows. The source evidence depends on real intervals, thresholds, and historically distinct layers. [P02-05](https://www.nps.gov/prsf/planyourvisit/infantry-row.htm), [P02-06](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-342-MPGuidelines_20110607.pdf), [P02-08](https://www.parks.ca.gov/pages/1054/files/2015_GovHPAwds_PresidioOfficers%27Club.pdf)

2. An imported regional palette. Phoenix’s rendered colors, BIO4’s timber story, or a desert artwork are not Presidio material specifications. Derive local choices from observed light, built fabric, and repair evidence. [P05-01](https://menlo-digital.com/portfolio/md-phx1-phoenix/), [P05-05](https://gottliebpaludan.com/en/projects/amager-power-station-blok-4), [P06-09](https://qm.org.qa/en/visit/public-art/richard-serra-east-west-west-east/), [P04-05](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-342-PresChapHSR_20120309.pdf)

3. Concealing scale in the presentation. Do not rely on aerial views, fog, cropped façades, or mature trees. Show the whole extent, public eye-level views, and planting-day conditions from consistent cameras. [P01-08](https://www.nps.gov/prsf/learn/nature/climate.htm), [P01-09](https://www.sfomuseum.org/exhibitions/san-francisco-david-rumsey-map-collection/gallery), [P01-06](https://presidio.gov/about/sustainability/creating-a-sustainable-forest), [P06-09](https://qm.org.qa/en/visit/public-art/richard-serra-east-west-west-east/)

4. Green fragments presented as ecological continuity. Do not assume many landscaped gaps outperform a compact footprint. Preserve habitat and water connections, and show construction disturbance as part of the proposal. [P01-07](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-344-VmpEa_200112-1.pdf), [P03-04](https://dot.ca.gov/-/media/dot-media/programs/risk-strategic-management/documents/mm-2016-q2-project-spotlight-a11y.pdf), [P03-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wd6RdaAQjZ8), [P03-08](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Tennessee-Hollow-Watershed-Walk-Accessible-June2023.pdf)

5. Beauty presented as consent or verified performance. Do not infer local endorsement, Indigenous permission, lower noise, clean energy, or safe access from reference images. The Northern Virginia report, public-space precedents, and Southern Cross complaints require narrower claims. [P02-01](https://www.ramaytush.org/original-peoples.html), [P05-03](https://www.gensler.com/gri/empowering-communities-with-data-center-design), [P03-01](https://www.fieldoperations.net/project/presidio-tunnel-tops), [P05-09](https://grimshaw.global/projects/rail-and-mass-transit/southern-cross-station/)

blocks.title: Wind Register — opportunity brief
blocks.content:
W&W synthesis — not an external source.

Expressive opportunity. Research brief, not a final building concept.

Thesis: Develop an expressive sequence from a restrained repeated element, calibrated to terrain, horizon, light, and the experience of moving past it.

Source observations: Wood Line turns incrementally; Spire changes against growing trees. Irwin’s UCSD mesh holds a level line above falling ground. GIS shells demonstrate folded repetition, while Serra warns that sparse elements can still dominate a vast landscape.

Design moves — our interpretation:

1. Keep technical modules legible, then vary one outer rib or folded-shell system through controlled changes in direction or depth.
2. Use a surveyed horizontal datum to reveal terrain variation; preserve important horizon openings instead of filling every gap.
3. Compare the complete silhouette from paths and distant overlooks in clear light, fog, and young planting conditions.

Tradeoff: Repeated expressive elements can amplify scale. Irwin’s added stays and Spire’s repair history require structural and maintenance scrutiny; neither artwork supplies an engineering solution.

Evidence: [P01-02](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/batteries-to-bluffs-trail), [P01-08](https://www.nps.gov/prsf/learn/nature/climate.htm), [P06-01](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/andy-goldsworthys-wood-line), [P06-02](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/andy-goldsworthys-spire), [P06-10](https://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/artist/irwin.html), [P05-06](https://www.cfmoller.com/p/GIS-buildings-i2654.html), [P06-08](https://www.sugimotohiroshi.com/seascapes-1), [P06-09](https://qm.org.qa/en/visit/public-art/richard-serra-east-west-west-east/).

blocks.title: Ground First — opportunity brief
blocks.content:
W&W synthesis — not an external source.

Landscape-led opportunity. Research brief, not a final building concept.

Thesis: Let continuous habitat, water routes, and public movement define what must stay open before assigning the building footprint.

Source observations: The vegetation plan values larger connected habitats; watershed mapping reveals water and paths as continuous systems. Crissy Field layers histories, while Quartermaster Reach shows that restoring connections required substantial infrastructure removal.

Design moves — our interpretation:

1. Map protected landscape relationships and necessary crossings first; compare compact and separated footprints against the same map.
2. Use sections to test roof edges against valley and bay views; distinguish any public deck from planted surface and equipment access.
3. Draw construction disturbance, drainage routes, and maintenance corridors alongside the proposed final landscape.

Tradeoff: A large industrial program may conflict with the very continuity being studied. A planted roof cannot replace intact habitat or validate structure, water management, public access, or land availability.

Evidence: [P01-01](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Trails-Map-Accessible.pdf), [P01-04](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/inspiration-point-overlook), [P01-07](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-344-VmpEa_200112-1.pdf), [P03-01](https://www.fieldoperations.net/project/presidio-tunnel-tops), [P03-02](https://www.hargreaves.com/work/crissy-field/), [P03-04](https://dot.ca.gov/-/media/dot-media/programs/risk-strategic-management/documents/mm-2016-q2-project-spotlight-a11y.pdf), [P03-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wd6RdaAQjZ8), [P03-08](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Tennessee-Hollow-Watershed-Walk-Accessible-June2023.pdf), [P03-10](https://www.architecturalecologies.cca.edu/research/presidio-culvert-reef), [P04-07](https://www.fondazionerenzopiano.org/en/project/california-academy-of-sciences/).

blocks.title: The Inhabited Screen — opportunity brief
blocks.content:
W&W synthesis — not an external source.

Contemporary opportunity. Research brief, not a final building concept.

Thesis: Place a purposeful, spatially deep outer layer around clear technical volumes. Let walking, shade, and changing views give that layer its architectural role.

Source observations: Funston’s porches and the East Mason frame establish local intervals and thresholds. Wood Line changes through walking. BIO4 puts an actual stair in its screen depth; de Young and Asawa offer distinct light-and-shadow studies.

Design moves — our interpretation:

1. Keep a straight operational enclosure and test a separate outer layer with measurable depth and replaceable parts.
2. Concentrate public routes and pauses in a few staffed, useful sections of that layer, with a separate secure boundary.
3. Prototype several fin intervals and orientations; compare shadow and apparent solidity from fixed ground-level cameras.

Tradeoff: A second layer adds cost, inspection, fire, wind, and maintenance questions. It cannot be assumed to reduce noise, improve cooling, or make a secure campus publicly accessible.

Evidence: [P02-04](https://www.nps.gov/places/000/funston-avenue-officers-family-housing.htm), [P04-04](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/NR_2022-NHPA-Annual-Report-FIN-notaccessible.pdf), [P06-01](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/andy-goldsworthys-wood-line), [P04-06](https://www.herzogdemeuron.com/projects/173-de-young-museum/), [P04-09](https://www.craigsteely.com/project/peters-house/), [P05-04](https://www.benthemcrouwel.com/projects/data-centers-equinix), [P05-05](https://gottliebpaludan.com/en/projects/amager-power-station-blok-4), [P06-05](https://ruthasawa.com/asawas-gift-to-sf-de-young-museum-2005/).

blocks.title: Porch, Court, and Bay — opportunity brief
blocks.content:
W&W synthesis — not an external source.

Tradition-informed opportunity. Research brief, not a final building concept.

Thesis: Use the Presidio’s spatial order of repeated buildings, generous intervals, sheltered fronts, and common ground to make the campus understandable at walking speed.

Source observations: Funston establishes an intentional public frontage; Infantry Row and the Main Post guidelines show why separate volumes and shared open ground matter. Fort Point adds a courtyard and deep repeated bays.

Design moves — our interpretation:

1. Compare a series of operational bars around genuine courts, with cross-views drawn through the gaps.
2. Place staffed rooms and sheltered entrances along a smaller public edge; draw secure service access separately.
3. Use one consistent bay interval and stepped roof datum, with contemporary joints that make new construction legible.

Tradeoff: Separation consumes land and can fragment habitat. Compare a compact alternative before treating the historical rhythm as the answer; decorative windows cannot substitute for actual gaps.

Evidence: [P02-04](https://www.nps.gov/places/000/funston-avenue-officers-family-housing.htm), [P02-05](https://www.nps.gov/prsf/planyourvisit/infantry-row.htm), [P02-06](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-342-MPGuidelines_20110607.pdf), [P02-08](https://www.parks.ca.gov/pages/1054/files/2015_GovHPAwds_PresidioOfficers%27Club.pdf), [P04-01](https://www.loc.gov/resource/hhh.ca0649.photos.016829p), [P04-02](https://www.nps.gov/goga/learn/historyculture/upload/2006-fopo-hsr.pdf), [P05-08](https://crossness.org.uk/gallery/).

blocks.title: Material and atmosphere palette — observation before specification
blocks.content:
W&W synthesis — not an external source.

Observed local palette: pale fog against darker land; warm roof colors and light wall planes at the coast; red brick and white porch elements at Infantry Row; gray-green fractured serpentinite; pale boardwalk against low dune planting. These are observations from selected images, not a universal Presidio color standard. [P01-08](https://www.nps.gov/prsf/learn/nature/climate.htm), [P02-05](https://www.nps.gov/prsf/planyourvisit/infantry-row.htm), [P01-10](https://www.nps.gov/prsf/learn/nature/serpentinite.htm), [P01-05](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/lobos-creek-valley-trail)

Observed depth and texture: brick vault courses, exposed timber framing, repaired log joints, terra-cotta projections, and the layered cut of Earth Wall. Different surfaces carry different maintenance histories. [P04-01](https://www.loc.gov/resource/hhh.ca0649.photos.016829p), [P04-04](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/NR_2022-NHPA-Annual-Report-FIN-notaccessible.pdf), [P04-03](https://presidio.gov/about/press/presidios-historic-log-cabin-getting-a-facelift), [P04-05](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-342-PresChapHSR_20120309.pdf), [P06-03](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/andy-goldsworthys-earth-wall)

Nearby comparisons: the de Young archive verifies copper mock-ups; the Academy archive separates planted roof, canopy, and skylight; Peter & Jan’s House documents movable louvers made from Presidio-reclaimed lumber. Their materials and mechanisms are evidence about those works, not ready specifications for this campus. [P04-06](https://www.herzogdemeuron.com/projects/173-de-young-museum/), [P04-07](https://www.fondazionerenzopiano.org/en/project/california-academy-of-sciences/), [P04-09](https://www.craigsteely.com/project/peters-house/)

Proposed use — our interpretation: test a restrained base palette through a few large samples and one full-scale edge mock-up. Compare a light solid wall, a darker recessed layer, and a replaceable outer screen under clear and diffuse light. Record drainage, access, repair, and source provenance alongside color. Never specify serpentinite from its appearance or assume reclaimed material exists at campus quantities. [P01-10](https://www.nps.gov/prsf/learn/nature/serpentinite.htm), [P04-03](https://presidio.gov/about/press/presidios-historic-log-cabin-getting-a-facelift), [P04-05](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-342-PresChapHSR_20120309.pdf)

blocks.title: Presidio design DNA — ten principles and tensions
blocks.content:
W&W synthesis — not an external source.

1. Preserve the landscape mosaic. Army-planted forest, native grassland, dunes, and marsh are different systems. A single planting formula would erase those differences. [P01-05](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/lobos-creek-valley-trail), [P01-06](https://presidio.gov/about/sustainability/creating-a-sustainable-forest), [P01-07](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-344-VmpEa_200112-1.pdf)

2. Draw the gaps before the façades. Main Post rows depend on common ground and bay views. Keep actual intervals visible in plan and ordinary views. [P02-05](https://www.nps.gov/prsf/planyourvisit/infantry-row.htm), [P02-06](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-342-MPGuidelines_20110607.pdf)

3. Test permeability against habitat continuity. Separate bars can improve walking routes while fragmenting habitat. Compare a compact footprint with a dispersed arrangement. [P01-07](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-344-VmpEa_200112-1.pdf), [P03-08](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Tennessee-Hollow-Watershed-Walk-Accessible-June2023.pdf)

4. Make the public edge useful. Porches, benches, crossings, and restrooms belong to a complete route. A security boundary still requires its own plan. [P02-04](https://www.nps.gov/places/000/funston-avenue-officers-family-housing.htm), [P03-01](https://www.fieldoperations.net/project/presidio-tunnel-tops), [P03-06](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/battery-bluff)

5. Keep history layered and accurately named. The current Officers’ Club includes later alterations. Ramaytush authorship and EXCLUSION prevent a decorative military-only narrative. [P02-01](https://www.ramaytush.org/original-peoples.html), [P02-08](https://www.parks.ca.gov/pages/1054/files/2015_GovHPAwds_PresidioOfficers%27Club.pdf), [P02-10](https://presidio.gov/special-exhibition-exclusion)

6. Use depth to make repetition legible. Vaults, timber frames, and occupied screens give scale through structure, shadow, and movement. [P04-01](https://www.loc.gov/resource/hhh.ca0649.photos.016829p), [P04-04](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/NR_2022-NHPA-Annual-Report-FIN-notaccessible.pdf), [P05-05](https://gottliebpaludan.com/en/projects/amager-power-station-blok-4)

7. Detail the water path. Cracked terra cotta and failed log chinking show why projections, joints, and replacements belong in the palette discussion. [P04-03](https://presidio.gov/about/press/presidios-historic-log-cabin-getting-a-facelift), [P04-05](https://wp.presidio.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PLN-342-PresChapHSR_20120309.pdf)

8. Compare clear, foggy, day, and night conditions. Atmosphere changes contrast; it must not conceal real size in the only presentation image. [P01-08](https://www.nps.gov/prsf/learn/nature/climate.htm), [P06-06](https://www.exploratorium.edu/sites/default/files/pdfs/over-the-water-catalog-nakaya.pdf), [P06-08](https://www.sugimotohiroshi.com/seascapes-1)

9. Design for changing care needs. Forest renewal, damaged artworks, and adjustable research panels make maintenance visible in the precedent record. [P01-06](https://presidio.gov/about/sustainability/creating-a-sustainable-forest), [P06-02](https://presidio.gov/explore/attractions/andy-goldsworthys-spire), [P03-10](https://www.architecturalecologies.cca.edu/research/presidio-culvert-reef)

10. Separate appearance from outcomes. A roof, screen, or public-space rendering cannot prove noise reduction, environmental performance, approval, or permission to build. [P05-03](https://www.gensler.com/gri/empowering-communities-with-data-center-design), [P05-09](https://grimshaw.global/projects/rail-and-mass-transit/southern-cross-station/)

blocks.title: 06 — An industrial mesh sharpens a planted grove
blocks.description:
Chapter 06 — Art and unexpected connections

Location: Eucalyptus grove between Faculty Club and Price Center, UC San Diego, La Jolla, California (external); status: built.

Observed / documented: The collection describes two elevated V-shaped structures of blue-violet coated chain-link mesh on stainless steel poles. Their elevation remains constant while the hillside falls. The inspected diptych shows a clear path beneath the mesh; the original sketch exposes its planar bends, supports, and bracing.

Design implication — our interpretation: Our interpretation: Investigate a layered screen that changes legibility with angle and light while preserving an uninterrupted public route. Use a surveyed level datum and slight changes of direction to connect repeated elements to the existing planted geometry.

Relevance and limit: External campus artwork, not a security fence. The primary essay records initial sagging and added stays. Neither its coating nor its ice-plant palette should be imported without local assessment.

blocks.title: 06 — Four narrow elements can command a kilometre
blocks.description:
Chapter 06 — Art and unexpected connections

Location: Brouq / Borouq Nature Reserve, western Qatar (external); status: built.

Observed / documented: Qatar Museums describes four steel plates, each over fourteen metres high, aligned after studying the terrain across more than a kilometre. Its photograph places human figures beside the repeated plates. The museum’s learning sheet dates the work to 2014.

Design implication — our interpretation: Our interpretation: Use sparse vertical elements only after studying their collective reading from multiple distances. Test the voids and intervals between masses as carefully as the individual objects; repetition can intensify perceived scale even when each element is slender.

Relevance and limit: External desert artwork, not a Presidio material palette or development model. This reference warns that low material quantity does not mean low visual impact. Photographs do not establish how a data-center campus would be received.

blocks.title: 06 — An uninterrupted horizon exposes changes in tone
blocks.description:
Chapter 06 — Art and unexpected connections

Location: Caribbean Sea, Jamaica (1980), and Ligurian Sea, Saviore (1993), as captioned by the artist (external); status: not-applicable.

Observed / documented: The artist’s page presents and captions three seascapes. In the inspected Caribbean Sea, Jamaica image, a sharp horizontal boundary separates pale sky from textured dark water. In Ligurian Sea, Saviore, the boundary becomes diffuse. The geometry stays spare while tonal definition changes substantially.

Design implication — our interpretation: Our interpretation: Frame selected sky and water views through deliberate gaps between masses. Compare the same proposed opening with high and low contrast so that a design depends on actual view geometry rather than a single atmospheric rendering.

Relevance and limit: External photographic analogy, not Presidio weather documentation. The inspected photographs were made in Jamaica and Italy. Their stillness and controlled framing cannot stand in for pedestrian experience or measured visibility.

blocks.title: 06 — Military traces become a sequence of light
blocks.description:
Chapter 06 — Art and unexpected connections

Location: Former army hospital site, Chinati Foundation, Marfa, Texas (external); status: built.

Observed / documented: Chinati documents a newly constructed building completed in 2016, cut into the slope with the former army hospital’s site relationship. Raised sills frame land and sky. Black and white scrims divide long wings. Alex Marks’s interior photograph shows repeated windows filtering through a translucent plane.

Design implication — our interpretation: Our interpretation: Use the distinction between structure, inner enclosure, and outer screen to tune a long elevation. Where public space is appropriate, make a sequence of framed landscape views rather than one continuous display window.

Relevance and limit: External artwork in West Texas; this is not a retained hospital shell. Its scrim and daylight effects are perceptual analogies, not evidence about thermal performance, industrial operations, or Presidio preservation compliance.

blocks.title: 06 — Engineered fog makes air movement visible
blocks.description:
Chapter 06 — Art and unexpected connections

Location: Bridge between Piers 15 and 17, Embarcadero, San Francisco (nearby-city); status: built.

Observed / documented: The catalog’s pages 10–11 describe weather readings and computer-controlled water nozzles responding to wind at Fog Bridge. This is engineered mist, not naturally arriving coastal fog. An original Exploratorium photograph shows bright mist against the dark pier structure and water, making contrast central to visibility.

Design implication — our interpretation: Our interpretation: Test façade depth and tonal contrast in clear, overcast, and foggy conditions from the same viewpoints. Let the study reveal how atmosphere changes perception of the enclosure and its edges.

Relevance and limit: Nearby-city art in a different microclimate. The 2013 catalog documents an installation, not current operating performance. It provides no evidence for cooling savings, safe visibility, or fog as an acceptable way to hide building mass.

blocks.title: 06 — Wire contains space while its shadow makes another layer
blocks.description:
Chapter 06 — Art and unexpected connections

Location: Hamon Observation Tower, de Young Museum, Golden Gate Park, San Francisco (nearby-city); status: built.

Observed / documented: The estate’s audio transcript describes the interaction of wire forms and shifting shadows, and Asawa’s selection of fifteen sculptures for a publicly accessible part of the museum. Randy Dodson’s installation photograph shows suspended forms overlapping their shadows on a concrete wall.

Design implication — our interpretation: Our interpretation: Study a ventilated screen as two perceptible layers: the screen itself and its changing shadow on the enclosure behind it. Vary separation and opening size through physical or lighting studies before settling on a pattern.

Relevance and limit: Nearby-city art, outside the Presidio. Fine wire sculpture does not verify façade structure, airflow, security, or maintenance. Family testimony about access does not establish public acceptance of industrial development.

blocks.title: 06 — A small military room becomes a slow visual threshold
blocks.description:

blocks.title: Orientation — architecture shaped by the Presidio
blocks.content:
W&W synthesis — not an external source.

How could a very large industrial program respond to a beloved public landscape with care, craft, and belonging? Use this board to study the place before choosing a formal language.

Read six chapters: 01 Ground and atmosphere; 02 Histories and built fabric; 03 Landscape as civic space; 04 Materials and craft; 05 Infrastructure; 06 Art and unexpected connections. Each reference separates documented observation, our design interpretation, and the limits of that transfer. Source IDs connect the board to the portable research package.

This is a speculative park study. The conceptual 1 GW campus, 275-acre study extent, and 7 million ft² floor area are internal comparison assumptions. They do not establish engineering requirements, available land, development rights, local support, or environmental benefits. No prepared site polygon was supplied; locations are labeled by park, subarea, adjacent context, or external precedent.
